To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
VSI is a spectro-imager that will provide the first images in the near-in- fra-red of compact sources with angular resolutions down to 3 milli-arcsec and spectral resolutions up to 100000.

(a) the VSI is an instrument capable to perform spectro-imaging at the VLTI with the UTs, the ATs or the future ELTs; (b) the VSI can probe compact sources in the near-infra-red domain at milli-arcseconds scales; (c) the VSI will be a unique instrument for the study of the physics of compact sources in the ELT era.

VSI will provide: - Spectroscopic information at milli-arcsec scales in the near infrared domain, - Spectral information at the diffraction limit of a 40 m class telescope, - A spectral resolution up to 100 000, - An angular resolution down to 2 milli-arcsec, - A field of view of 2.5 x 2.5 arcsec^2, - A wavelength range from 1.2 to 2.4 microns,
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following scientific themes: - The study of the physical properties of circumstellar disks in which planets form, and the search for the earliest stages of planet formation.

the following scientific objectives:   1. to investigate the formation and evolution of stars from early to late stages   2. to understand the formation of planetary systems and the origin of life   3. to study the physics of accretion disks around young stars and active galactic nuclei The main goal of the instrument is to provide milli-arcsecond resolution in both spatial and spectral dimensions.
the development of a spectro-imager for the VLTI that will allow us to investigate the physics and chemistry of a large variety of objects in our Galaxy and in nearby galaxies.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the VSI is the only instrument able to provide a complete picture of the sources in the near-in-frared domain at milli-arcsec resolution.
the VSI is a key instrument for a full understanding of the physical processes in compact objects, which are the main actors of stellar evolution and the birth and evolution of galaxies.
the VSI will allow us to probe the innermost regions of the most interesting sources in our Galaxy, the Milky Way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
VSI is a powerful spectro-imager that can provide a unique and unprecedented view of the Universe.
we have designed a spectro-imager that will be a key instrument for the future ELT.

VSI will be a key tool to investigate the physics and chemistry in a wide range of objects, such as the circumstellar environments of evolved stars, the disks of young stars, the innermost region of AGN and the atmospheres of exoplanets.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the combination of a spectro-imager with a long baseline interferometer will provide a unique tool for the study of the most compact sources in the Universe.
VSI will provide a unique and complementary capability in the context of the next decade of ground based astronomy.
VSI is a very efficient instrument for the study of compact objects, in particular, the ones with extended envelopes.
